cards.explanation: The answer is clean, friends. The man says, “If You are willing, You can make me clean.” (Mark 1:40) He doesn't ask for a little help or a nicer week. He asks for the whole thing, and he asks it on his knees.

The answer is “If You are willing.” The man says, “If You are willing, You can make me clean.” (Mark 1:40) He says Jesus can make him clean, and the "if" is about whether Jesus is willing. I think that's a humble way to ask.

The answer is True. Mark says, “Moved with compassion, Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man.” (Mark 1:41) Compassion moves Him, and His hand reaches out. Then He tells the man He is willing. I think this is a tender moment.
The answer is True, and there's no waiting around. “And immediately the leprosy left him, and the man was cleansed.” (Mark 1:42) No second visit, no follow-up appointment. Jesus speaks and it's done.

The word is tell, friends. Jesus says, “See that you don’t tell anyone.” (Mark 1:44) That's a big ask when you've just been healed. It's like getting the best news of your life and being told to keep it out of the group chat.
The answer is the priest. Jesus says, “But go, show yourself to the priest…” (Mark 1:44) So the man isn't told to just keep quiet and wander off. He's given a place to go.
The answer is a testimony. Jesus says to present the offering Moses prescribed “…as a testimony to them.” (Mark 1:44) Mark doesn't say more about who "them" is. So I'll leave it right there.

The answer is False, bakers. The text says, “But the man went out and openly began to proclaim and spread the news.” (Mark 1:45) Jesus told him not to tell anyone. He spread the news anyway, and he did it openly.

The answer is that Jesus can't enter a town in plain view. Mark says, “Consequently, Jesus could no longer enter a town in plain view…” (Mark 1:45) The news travels, and it changes where Jesus can go. Plain view is out.

The answer is that people come to Him from every quarter. “Yet people came to Him from every quarter.” (Mark 1:45) Jesus is out in solitary places, and folks still find Him. Even the quiet spots get busy!
